name: The Saturday Loaf
headline: Order by Thursday. Warm by Saturday.
intro: One oven, one baker, six bakes a weekend. Reserve what you'd like before the Thursday cut-off and collect it from the side gate on Saturday — still warm if you take the early slot.
about: The Saturday Loaf is me, Ida, a spreadsheet analyst on weekdays and a baker from Friday teatime onwards. Everything is mixed, proved, and baked in my registered home kitchen — small batches, long fermentation, no shortcuts. I bake exactly what has been ordered plus a couple of spares, which is why the list closes on Thursday and why the slots genuinely run out.
collectionNote: Collection is from the side gate — follow the smell of bread and the painted arrow.

faqs.question: How do I pay?
faqs.answer: At collection — contactless card or cash at the gate. The order email only reserves your bakes; no money changes hands online.

faqs.question: What happens after I send the order email?
faqs.answer: You get a short reply confirming your bakes and slot, usually within a few hours. If a slot fills before your email lands, we offer you the nearest free one instead.

faqs.question: What if I miss my collection slot?
faqs.answer: Reply to your confirmation or send a text and we will hold your bag until the last slot of the day ends. After that, unclaimed bakes are offered to the waiting list.

faqs.question: Is everything sourdough?
faqs.answer: The breads are — naturally leavened with a rye starter and proved slowly in the fridge. The knots, babka, and cake use yeast or baking powder where it simply tastes better.

faqs.question: Do you list allergens?
faqs.answer: Every bake comes from one small kitchen that handles gluten, nuts, dairy, eggs, sesame, and soy, so nothing can be guaranteed trace-free. Ask about any bake and you will get the full ingredient list by reply.
